title: e Bay Inc (EBAY) Deep Dive Analysis
summary: Fiscal dependence and e Bay consolidation.
coverage_note: All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

claims.reason: BEA recorded rising transfers and income despite lost employment, supporting the buffer. Currency depreciation is not a mechanical consequence of every fiscal expansion, and simultaneous reopening also affects spending.

evidence.title: May 2020 personal income and outlays
evidence.finding: Personal income fell 4.2% in May after revised 10.8% growth in April. Declining recovery payments explained much of the decrease, partly offset by unemployment benefits. Spending rose 8.2%.

evidence.title: June 2022 Consumer Price Index
evidence.finding: June 2022 headline CPI rose 9.1% over twelve months.

claims.reason: Finalized Texas data corroborate the southern-US improvement. This does not independently establish each comparison with Brazil, India, Europe and East Asia or contemporary reporting definitions.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.

evidence.title: Historical Texas dashboard data
evidence.finding: Archived Trends sheet Total Fatalities Current Day: seven-day averages ending July 5, July 19, August 2, August 16, August 30, 2020 were 118.00,242.14,233.29,179.43,108.14. Later-vintage data, not contemporary reporting snapshots.

evidence.title: PPP Flexibility Act implementation
evidence.finding: Forgiveness covered period extended to 24 weeks; prior borrowers could elect eight weeks. Loan maturity was distinct, generally two or five years, not end-June 2020.

evidence.title: July 2020 employment situation
evidence.finding: Payrolls rose 1.8 m in July after 4.8 m in June and 2.7 m in May; unemployment fell to 10.2%. Permanent job losers were approximately unchanged at 2.9 m in July; temporary layoffs fell 1.3 m.

evidence.title: COVID-19 oversight report
evidence.finding: GAO found continued-claim totals counted weeks, not unique beneficiaries. DOL clarified this in December 2020; backlogs could produce several weeks per person in one report.

evidence.title: All about the business cycle
evidence.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St Louis
evidence.finding: The NBER-dated COVID recession lasted two months, with February 2020 peak and April trough. Ending contraction does not imply immediate recovery to prior output or employment levels.

claims.reason: Payrolls did not recover the February 2020 level until July 2022. That supports the slow-recovery warning, although the technological-acceleration causal explanation is not identified.

evidence.title: July 2022 Employment Situation release

claims.reason: The stated sustained-withdrawal condition was interrupted by subsequent relief and direct checks. Fiscal sensitivity is plausible, but the counterfactual cannot be credited as an observed recession.

claims.reason: Large repurchases and dividends continued, supporting capacity. Yet 2025 payouts exceeded that year's free cash flow; divestiture proceeds, debt and accumulated cash matter. Do not extrapolate a perpetual payout from one profitable year.

claims.reason: The first five-year checkpoint delivered about 13.89% annualized, exceeding the discussion's 10% valuation hurdle. It lagged SPY, so this is an absolute-return success, not market-beating selection. Longer continuation remains open.

framework_lessons: Separate divestiture gains from recurring earnings.
assessment: The long-horizon e Bay investment produced solid absolute returns, though below SPY. Its operating turnaround was uneven and the GAAP earnings path failed. The major fiscal compromise came after the election. The dated Bitcoin view succeeded; open-ended gold and valuation views need explicit failure conditions.
verification_limitations: Retrieved 2026-11-07; publication-date wording is not authenticated.
